title: The payer’s letter uploaded in “Log a payer response”
assertion: The form shows with no letter on file; the letter goes through the same scanned intake; what was typed before the upload keeps its value through the scan and the page read again; the letter is chosen only once it is stored, and only the letter that form uploaded or, for a duplicate, the copy on file a response may carry, never over the person’s own choice, and the choice never moves focus; a duplicate it does not choose is named by when its copy was uploaded, as its option starts; the letter that form uploaded starts “Uploaded here” in the list, and every option starts with what tells it apart; an empty or too large letter is refused in one file’s words, never told to zip it; a press while it uploads or is scanned sends nothing; a stored letter the list does not show yet is said to be on its way, and if it never arrives the form says to reload; no button of the uploader submits the form; leaving the page asks only while the letter is being sent, a Retry that sends it again included, and never at the press that records the response; where the person cannot upload or uploads are paused or closed, the card says to choose a letter on file, or, with none on file, that no response can be recorded yet, and the uploader’s panel says why under a title true to the state, in an upload’s words; the drop zone is named by its heading; a file dropped on the form, with nothing typed, is cleared with the form for another person signed in on the same browser; the letter’s field and its upload sit under headings one level below the form’s, and the rest of the form under a heading of its own; no request carries the file’s name, and no upload request carries the form’s request key; the submission log names each response’s letter and links its receipt
noFileReason: A SYNTHETIC payer letter the test builds as a PDF and uploads in the browser: no file.
